ImageDescription.value:
Freddie Mercury performing at New Haven Coliseum in New Haven, CT

Photography in portrait format, in color. Freddie's upper body from the waist to the head takes up the entire image. In his right hand, he holds a microphone in front of his open mouth and sings. The microphone is attached to an about 1-meter-long stand, which was removed from the lower holder. His head is slightly inclined to the back and to the right, so the left half of his face is turned toward the viewer. Freddie's left eye is half-closed. His left hand is loosely spread and his left index finger elegantly carries the microphone cable at neck level. Freddie is shaved and wears a five o'clock shadow. The backcombed dark brown mullet is lit from behind, creating a thin yellow glowing outline around the head. Between the hair and the left sideburns, the earlobe can be seen. He wears a tight white bodysuit with hand-sized black diamonds. The very deep oval neckline exposes much of the hairy torso almost to the navel. Two large black diamonds extend below the neckline, touching at the inner corners and connected with more diamonds at the outer corners. The diamond pattern of the full bodysuit is reminiscent of a harlequin. The diamonds at the elbows are slimmer and occupy half the forearm of the ¾ sleeve. The held microphone cable and the stand form an X in front of Freddie's bare chest.

The background is reddish-brown. Under Freddie's right elbow, parts of two drum cymbals can be blurredly seen. Freddie is completely in his element and is devoted to the music. His body language and facial expression make one feel that Freddie is sensually absorbed in the music.

ImageDescription.value:
Freddie Mercury (5 September 1946 – 24 November 1991) was a British singer, songwriter and producer, best known as the lead vocalist and lyricist of the rock band Queen.

As a member of Queen, he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2001, the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2003, the UK Music Hall of Fame in 2004, and the band received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2002.

The statue stands almost 10 feet (3 metres) high overlooking Lake Geneva.
